title: Remission is free, not merited by inherent justice
source_text: XXXVI. Sicut autem sanctitas & justitia illa, quam fidelibus indit Spiritus Sanctus, non obstat quominus egeant divina clementia, & misericordia, ad remissionem pec-catorum suorum, tam quae admiserunt ante suam justificationem, quam quae post illam quotidie admittunt: ita quoque remissio illa, respectu nostri, plane gratuita est; nec putandum est Deum nos in gratiam recipere, & peccata nobis condonare, pro-pter justitiam ullam quae nobis inest, sive propter illa opera, quibus ad veram justi-tiam & sanctitatem disponimur: quasi opera quaedam nostra aut justitia nobis per Spiritum Sanctum impressa, meritoria essent remissionis peccatorum nostrorum.
pass_a_gloss: But as that holiness and righteousness which the Holy Spirit implants in believers does not prevent their needing divine clemency and mercy for the remission of their sins, both those they committed before their justification and those they daily commit after it: so also that remission, with respect to us, is plainly free; nor is it to be thought that God receives us into grace and pardons our sins because of any righteousness that is in us, or because of those works by which we are disposed to true righteousness and holiness—as if certain works of ours or righteousness impressed on us by the Holy Spirit were meritorious of the remission of our sins.
pass_b_english: Inherent holiness does not remove need of free pardon for sins before and after justification.
Remission is not merited by any justice or preparatory works in us.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1070.
